speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to help me understand what's causing this, could you tell me how long the ulcer has been present and if you have noticed any fever or chills recently? Also, do you have any history of diabetes, venous insufficiency, or recent insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent uveitis treatment with corticosteroids, we must rule out opportunistic infections like Disseminated Histoplasmosis or Pyoderma Gangrenosum, especially since you recall an ant bite. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Blood Glucose, and Fungal Serology (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides). REQUEST IMAGES: Please show me a clear photograph of the ulcer's base and borders.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The combination of a painful ulcer with a necrotic base and violaceous (purplish) borders in a patient with Crohn's disease and recent steroid use is classic for this neutrophilic dermatosis, despite the history of an ant bite. The presence of dilated veins and pitting edema suggests concurrent chronic venous insufficiency, which likely acted as a predisposing factor.
